TITLE: Contingent Value Rights
ALIASES:
DESCRIPTION: Covers rights granted by an acquirer to shareholders to manage transaction uncertainty.
SUMMARY: Contingent Value Rights are rights granted by an acquirer to shareholders to facilitate transactions with inherent uncertainty. These rights can be event-driven or price-protection based, and they help bridge negotiations. Shareholders receive additional compensation if a specific event occurs within a timeframe.
ORG: hedge funds || WHY: They occasionally acquire or short Contingent Value Rights securities.
ORG: Media General / Nexstar Media Group || WHY: Used as an example of where CVRs are common in the biotech and pharmaceutical industries.
ORG: FASB || WHY: Mentioned in relation to the valuation of intangible assets.
CONCEPT: Option
WHY: The CVR is in function as a form of option.
CONCEPT: Call option
WHY: The first case of CVRs is analogous to a call option.
CONCEPT: Asian option
WHY: The second type of CVR takes the form of a modified Asian option.
FACT: Event-driven CVRs compensate owners for positive developments in their business. || SECTION: Forms
FACT: Price-protection CVRs are granted when payment is share based. || SECTION: Forms
FACT: CVRs are common in the biotech and pharmaceutical industries. || SECTION: Forms
FACT: The payout to the CVR holder will be triggered by the event occurring and will be zero otherwise. || SECTION: Valuation
FACT: Analysts apply a modified option pricing model based on the probability of the event, time horizon, and payout rules. || SECTION: Valuation
